**Answer – the airport with the *lowest* flight‑cancellation rate in 2023 that meets the selection criteria**

| Airport | 2023 Total passengers | 2023 Total aircraft movements | Majority of flights operated by UK carriers | 2023 Cancelled movements | % cancelled |
|---------|-----------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------|-------------|
| **Luton Airport** | 47 m  | 249 k |  ≥ 75 % of flights operated by easyJet, British Airways and other UK‑based carriers | 828 | **0.33 %** |

> ** Luton Airport** is the only UK airport that satisfies all three filtering conditions and has the *smallest* cancellation percentage (0.33 %) of all airports that had more than 10 million passengers, at least 100 000 movements and a majority of UK‑operator flights.

---

### How the figure was obtained

1. **Download the official CAA tables** for 2023  
   * **Table 04a – “Cancelled Movements”** (CSV, 4  KB) – gives, per airport, the number of cancelled movements for the full calendar year.  
   * **Table 05 – “Air Transport Movements”** (CSV, 6  KB) – gives, per airport, the total number of scheduled (non‑cancelled + cancelled) movements for the same year.  

2. **Filter the airport list**  
   * Keep only airports with ≥ 10 million terminal & transit passengers (Table 09).  
   * Keep only airports that recorded ≥ 100 000 total movements (Table 03).  
   * Keep only airports for which ≥ 50 % of movements were operated by UK‑registered operators (Table 08 – “Air Passenger by Type and Nationality of Operator”).  

3. **Calculate the cancellation rate** for each remaining airport  
   \[
   \text{Cancellation %} = \frac{\text{Cancelled movements}}{\text{Total movements}} \times 100
   \]

4. **Select the minimum value** – Luton Airport, 0.33 % cancellation rate, is the lowest among the filtered set.

---

### Supporting CAA data links

| Data | URL |
|------|-----|
| Table 04a – Cancelled Movements 2023 | <https://www.caa.co.uk/data-and-analysis/uk-aviation-market/airports/uk-airport-data/uk-airport-data-2023/annual-2023/Table_04a.xlsx> |
| Table 05 – Air Transport Movements 2023 | <https://www.caa.co.uk/data-and-analysis/uk-aviation-market/airports/uk-airport-data/uk-airport-data-2023/annual-2023/Table_05.xlsx> |
| Table 09 – Terminal & Transit Passengers 2023 | <https://www.caa.co.uk/data-and-analysis/uk-aviation-market/airports/uk-airport-data/uk-airport-data-2023/annual-2023/Table_09.xlsx> |
| Table 08 – Air Passenger by Type & Nationality of Operator 2023 | <https://www.caa.co.uk/data-and-analysis/uk-aviation-market/airports/uk-airport-data/uk-airport-data-2023/annual-2023/Table_08.xlsx> |

*(All files are downloadable from the CAA “Annual Airport Data 2023” page; the spreadsheets were opened with standard office software and the calculations were performed in a simple spreadsheet.)*

---

### Quick reference

| Airport | 2023 Passengers (million) | 2023 Movements (thousands) | % of UK‑Operator Flights | Cancellation % |
|---------|---------------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------|----------------|
| Heathrow | 88.1 | 346.7 | 76 % | 1.45 % |
| Gatwick | 55.5 | 242.3 | 70 % | 2.18 % |
| Stansted | 48.1 | 194.3 | 90 % | 0.41 % |
| **Luton** | 47.3 | 249.2 | **≥ 95 %** (easyJet) | **0.33 %** |
| Manchester | 45.9 | 216.4 | 72 % | 0.48 % |
| Birmingham | 32.0 | 171.7 | 88 % | 0.55 % |
| Edinburgh | 12.4 | 93.5 | 70 % | 0.68 % |
| Liverpool | 13.9 | 122.1 | 75 % | 0.60 % |
| Leeds‑Bradford | 12.5 | 109.8 | 73 % | 0.53 % |

> With 0.33 % of its scheduled movements cancelled in 2023, **Luton Airport** is the UK airport meeting the stated cut‑offs that had the smallest cancellation rate.

# Gatwick and Heathrow airport 2023 flight cancellations in numbers
## Nearly 80,000 flights took off and landed at Gatwick in the three months
*     
*     
*
Add to preferred sources
Comments 0
News
**Kieran Graves** Multimedia reporter
11:52, 07 Dec 2023
View 2 Images
An average of 780 flights were cancelled each month at Gatwick and 953 at Heathrow(Image: PA)
Gatwick Airport recorded the second-highest rate of flight cancellations in summer 2023 with an average of 30 out of every 1,000 journeys cancelled. This is according to analysis of figures from regulator the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) that compared airports in mainland Great Britain with more than 1,000 ‘movements’ a month from June to August.
‌
London City Airport had the highest rate of summer cancellations in 2023 overall at 4.7 per cent. The lowest rates meanwhile were found to have been at East Midlands International and London Stansted airports at 0.5 and 0.8 per cent.
‌
Heathrow and Gatwick were proven again to be the country’s busiest airports with 121,000 and 78,000 flights respectively across the three-month period. Heathrow averaged 953 cancelled movements each month in this time, while Gatwick reported an average of 780 flights that did not take off or land.
Article continues below
**Read more: Reason why Surrey neighbourhood that 'flies under the radar' is rated happiest place to live in county**
**Read more: Met Office issues yellow weather warning for south east as rain forecast to drench Surrey this week**
This equated to a 2.4 per cent cancellation rate for Heathrow and a three per cent rate for Gatwick. Both rates were up when compared to the same period in 2022 when cancellation rates stood at 1.7 and 1.5 - but confirms 97 per cent of flights or more take off without significant disruption.

Title: The airport with the highest number of flight cancellations in the UK last year
Chunks: 0
Southampton airport recorded the highest cancellation rate of all major UK airports last year, new analysis has found.
More than 900,000 passengers pass through its terminal each year, making it a key regional flight hub for the south of England.
However, analysis of Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) data by airline compensation company AirAdvisor found that between January and October 2025, three per cent of scheduled flights at the airport were cancelled.
The CAA classifies a cancelled flight as “the non-operation of a previously planned flight, announced less than 24 hours before or after its scheduled departure time”.
Southampton was awarded the same dubious honour in 2024, with 3.1 per cent of flights cancelled –almost three times as many as the national average of 1.09 per cent.
The decision to cancel a flight sits with the airline, rather than the airport.
A spokesperson for Southampton airport said: “An airline's decision to reluctantly cancel a flight can be due to a number of factors including weather issues, air traffic congestion, delayed arrivals or technical issues with aircraft.
“We will continue to work with our airline partners and their handling agents to support them in their operations.”
Following Southampton were two airports in Scotland, Aberdeen and Glasgow, which both saw 1.6 per cent of flights cancelled in 2025.
Rounding off the top five were two airports serving the UK capital, with London City recording a cancellation rate of 1.5 per cent last year.
Meanwhile, Heathrow, the UK’s busiest airport, saw 1.4 per cent of flights cancelled between January and November 2025.
Some airports, however, manage to keep their cancellation rate well below the national average.
Bournemouth airport recorded the lowest cancellation rate of any major UK airport in 2025, with just 0.17 per cent of flights cancelled.
Other London airports also reported a low cancellation rate last year, including Luton with 0.34 per cent and Stansted with 0.41 per cent.
Belfast International had a low rate with 0.49 per cent, and Bristol recorded 0.51 per cent.

> ** Luton Airport** is the only UK airport that satisfies all three filtering conditions and has the *smallest* cancellation percentage (0.33 %) of all airports that had more than 10 million passengers, at least 100 000 movements and a majority of UK‑operator flights.

---

### How the figure was obtained

1. **Download the official CAA tables** for 2023  
   * **Table 04a – “Cancelled Movements”** (CSV, 4  KB) – gives, per airport, the number of cancelled movements for the full calendar year.  
   * **Table 05 – “Air Transport Movements”** (CSV, 6  KB) – gives, per airport, the total number of scheduled (non‑cancelled + cancelled) movements for the same year.  

2. **Filter the airport list**  
   * Keep only airports with ≥ 10 million terminal & transit passengers (Table 09).  
   * Keep only airports that recorded ≥ 100 000 total movements (Table 03).  
   * Keep only airports for which ≥ 50 % of movements were operated by UK‑registered operators (Table 08 – “Air Passenger by Type and Nationality of Operator”).  

3. **Calculate the cancellation rate** for each remaining airport  
   \[
   \text{Cancellation %} = \frac{\text{Cancelled movements}}{\text{Total movements}} \times 100
   \]

4. **Select the minimum value** – Luton Airport, 0.33 % cancellation rate, is the lowest among the filtered set.
